  • L mode: Type exact segment length for polylines.
  • Multi-view is supported — add views from the top bar.
Reference

Navigation & Shortcuts

Type a command. With a keyboard (a computer, or an iPad with one attached), start typing any tool's name with nothing selected in a box: Polyline, Move, Offset, Fillet, Dim, Crop, Save. A list of matches appears as you type, short names work too (L, M, O, J, X), and Enter, Space or Tab starts the top one. Arrow keys pick another, Escape closes it. Enter with no tool running repeats the last command. Not shown on phones.

Number boxes take units and math. A plain number is in the box's own units. You can also type another unit (25mm, 1/2", 2in, 1.5m), feet and inches (13' 6", 5ft 3in), or a sum (13x12, (2+3)*4mm, 10/4). It is worked out when you press Enter or leave the box, and the answer replaces what you typed.

Zoom: Scroll wheel or pinch. Anchors to cursor. Max 50×.

Pan: Space+drag, middle mouse, or two-finger drag.

Leaving a tool. Tap a lit tool button again to put it down and return to Select. A button with several modes (Circle, Rectangle, Edit Pts, Mirror/Symmetry, Scale, Align) steps through each mode once, and the next tap leaves it. If work is waiting on the ✓, you are asked first.

Keyboard shortcuts:

  • Ctrl+Z — Undo last action
  • Ctrl+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y — Redo
  • A letter — Opens the command line (desktop and iPad with a keyboard); type a tool's name and press Enter
  • Enter — Finish polyline or curve; with no tool running, repeat the last command
  • Escape — Cancel what is in progress; press again to leave the tool for Select, and again to deselect
  • Delete / Backspace — Delete selected geometry; while placing points, take back the last point
  • Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V — Copy / Paste
  • Ctrl+A — Select all
  • [ ] — Decrease / increase brush size
  • Ctrl (hold) — Momentary ortho toggle
  • Shift (hold) — Momentary snap toggle
  • Alt (hold) — Momentary guides toggle
  • CapsLock — Tap to toggle the loupe on/off; hold to show a hover loupe under the cursor without clicking
  • Space (hold) — Pan mode (drag to pan)
  • Right-click — Delete point in Edit mode. In Select mode, opens a popup to pick between overlapping geometry.
  • Long-press (mobile) — Same as right-click: pick between overlapping geometry when objects are stacked.

Troubleshooting

  • Perspective correction looks wrong: Check that you clicked points accurately. In Corner mode, the corner point (◆) must be exactly where the arms meet. Use the Loupe for precision placement.
  • Grid or straight lines still look wavy after correction: This is lens barrel distortion, not perspective. Calibrate a lens profile at the Camera Calibration page for your specific lens.
  • Scale is off: Use Dual Rulers for best accuracy — it corrects independent X and Y scale. Verify with the Measure tool on a known dimension.
  • Detection misses shapes: Use the Guide Brush to focus detection on specific areas. Improve contrast — dark object on light surface works best. Adjust Threshold and Detail sliders. Avoid shadows across the subject.
  • Reference sheet not detected: All 4 markers must be fully visible. Ensure good, even lighting with no glare on the sheet. If you can see all four and it still fails, use Place corners by hand (see Reference Sheet).
  • Large objects are distorted: Stand back and use telephoto (2×). Avoid ultrawide lens. Crouch to mid-height of the object.
  • Far legs / far edges look wrong on furniture: This is parallax — the near parts physically blocked the far parts from that camera angle. Shoot more head-on, or accept that a single photo can't capture deeply hidden geometry.
  • Lens Correction: Most iPhones pre-correct JPEGs. Leave at "None" unless you've calibrated a custom profile. If using a profile, always download a .lenscal backup — browser storage can be cleared.
  • Missing lens profile: If your profile disappears (browser data cleared, new device), import your .lenscal backup file from the upload screen.
  • HEIC files: Fully supported. Avoid screenshots — they strip EXIF metadata needed for lens profile matching.
  • The 3D model is the wrong size or shape: Open Details in the preview — it says what it assumed. The usual causes are a view whose outline did not close (draw the part as one closed outline, as closed shapes that touch, which are joined into one, or as separate closed shapes, which are paired across the views; use Clean Up or Snap Corners where pieces do not meet), a view labelled with the wrong side (Smart Trace offers to relabel it, or use the pencil beside the view list), a view photographed a quarter turn round, or leftover shapes drawn well outside the outline (the preview names them; delete them). Make views agree at the bottom of the view list checks whether the views measure the part the same, and fixes it. Turning the Photo overlay on shows which face is which straight away.
  • The STEP option is greyed out when you press Save model: Its tooltip says why — that server has no CAD kernel, so the preview is showing a voxel hull instead of the true solid. The 3DM, STL and OBJ still save (the 3DM file needs no kernel; STL and OBJ carry the stepped skin you can see on screen).
  • An OBJ opens as four copies of the part, like a cross: some phone viewers turn each material group separately, so the OBJ is written as one material over one image. If it still happens, save the 3DM file instead — it carries a true solid. (Some phone viewers do not show OBJ textures at all; desktop 3D programs do.)
  • DXF output: Opens at 1:1 scale in any CAD program that reads DXF. The corrected image is embedded as a background — trace over it or use the exported geometry directly.
  • The photo shows as an empty frame in CAD: the DXF refers to its photos by name, so keep them in the same folder as the .dxf when you unzip.
  • Reporting a problem: Report issue in the Help header sends us a note with what the app already knows attached. Debug bundle beside it downloads what we need to reproduce it: Small is the drawing only, a few KB, and is what usually works on a phone; Full includes the photos.
build b490

CAD

Draw to scale: a plan, a part, a pattern to cut out. Lines, arcs, circles and curves, with sizes typed in or measured. Save it, print it at true size, or hand it to a machine as a DXF. No internet needed.

Back to ARK

Open a drawing

Print the drawing

In the printer's own box, leave scaling at 100% (not "fit to page"), and pick the same paper. The line under the drawing has a bar to check with a ruler.

The basics: new, save, open, print

  1. New drawing: give the sheet a width and height a little bigger than what you will draw. You draw at real size: a line typed as 36 is 36 inches long.
  2. Draw (bottom left) opens the tools. Pick one, then tap or click on the sheet. Sizes can be typed in the boxes that appear. Dimension adds measurements, text and notes.
  3. File › Save keeps the drawing. On an ARK Vault or a library drive it goes to that drive, where everyone using the library can open it; anywhere else it is saved to your device as a file ending in .lcad.
  4. File › Print prints at true size (a pattern to cut round), to fit one sheet, or at a plan's scale such as 1/4 inch to the foot. A drawing bigger than the paper prints on several sheets to lay edge to edge. On an ARK Vault it can print on the receipt printer too, in strips to tape side by side.
  5. File › Save as DXF makes the file other CAD programs, laser cutters and CNC machines read.

The page also keeps the open drawing by itself every half minute, on this device. If the page closes or the power goes, Carry on on the first screen brings it back. That copy is a safety net, not a save: only one drawing is kept, and clearing the browser's data removes it.

Scroll or pinch to zoom, drag with two fingers (or hold Space) to move the sheet. Undo and Redo are in the top bar.
